mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month averages signals strengthening demand fundamentals, which boost earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month averages for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its 5-year average, without accompanying wage inflation, signals improved labor supply without cost pressure, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS exceeds 5-year average for three months
regime_hint: labor supply expansion without wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS exceeds its 5-year average for three consecutive months without wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month average, combined with a flat or declining consumption growth (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer confidence shock and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises above 12-month average for four consecutive months while GDPC1 is flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises above its 12-month average for four consecutive months while GDPC1 is flat or declining.
